gaps.quote: to the power of its selected bits equal to $1$
gaps.note: The page never says which bits are selected. Inferring that they are the D bits at the common offset is a guess, so S_D is not determined by the page.

The identity is asserted with 'Then'. The reader cannot check it: the page does not show the one-factor identity H_0 = ((1-i)/2) S C S, and does not say that S_D is the D-fold tensor power of diag(1, i).

gaps.quote: so the layer reduces to $C^{\otimes D}$
gaps.note: Exactness of scalars and phases does not by itself show that the layer reduces to C^{\otimes D}. The page does not say how the outer S_D factors are handled or why the reduction is valid.

gaps.quote: $C$ is not one: its row absolute sums are $\sqrt2$, so $C^{\otimes D}$ can enlarge values by up to $2^{D/2}$.
gaps.note: The page never states that a matrix's row absolute sums bound how much it can enlarge the maximum coefficient norm, nor that row sums multiply under tensor powers. The bound 2^{D/2} therefore cannot be checked.

gaps.term: unit row sums give exact run and one truncation
gaps.quote: $H_0$ has row absolute sums $1$, so the layer runs exactly and truncates once.
gaps.note: The page does not say that row sums of 1 make H_0 a contraction in the maximum norm, nor why no intermediate truncation is then needed. This depends on the unstated principle in the previous step.

gaps.quote: split into $m$ slots, the label-space dimension
gaps.note: The page does not say what a label space is or what a slot is. m is named as their count but not explained.
The page does not say what a wire role is. The sentence only gives W as their count. The linked role-streams page is about scheduling and is not linked for this term.

gaps.quote: Each level multiplies the volume by $s/W<m$
gaps.note: The inequality s/W < m is asserted without derivation, and this page does not link the result that establishes it (the rank-deficit page).

gaps.term: work as a power of group size
gaps.quote: so the work is a power of the group size with exponent $\max\{0,\log_m(s/W)\}<1$
gaps.note: The page gives no cost accounting: work per level equal to volume, depth log_m of the group size, a geometric sum over levels, and the dominant term. It also never relates the group size e to the chunk count D or the bound d, so the cited O(V d^{λ'}) time cannot be read off from this exponent.

gaps.quote: The layer uses $p+\Delta$ fractional bits and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per real component (cited).
gaps.note: This cited claim states how the layer's own arithmetic works. The page does not say why these widths hold all intermediate values, and the growth bounds it discusses (row sums) are not connected to the widths.

gaps.term: truncation keeps coefficients in the unit disk
gaps.quote: truncation toward zero to $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$ keeps coefficients in the unit disk, with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$ (cited).
gaps.note: The claim that truncated values stay in the unit disk requires that the values before truncation lie in the disk. The page never says which values are truncated or what bound they satisfy beforehand.
